newsitem.title: CANADA: Court dismisses Service Corp. suit against Loewen.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses Service Corp. suit against Loewen.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc. said Sunday that a Texas court granted its motion to dismiss a lawsuit by Service Corp. International, which has made a $2.9 billion hostile bid for its smaller funeral home rival.

Loewen said the ruling by the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas cleared the way for it to proceed with its antitrust lawsuit in New York federal court, challenging the proposed business combination of Service Corp. and Loewen.
Houston-based Service Corp. International, the largest funeral home and cemetery chain in North America, has offered to buy Lowen for $2.9 billion.
Loewen, a funeral services company based in Vancouver, British Columbia, and Service Corp.'s biggest rival, has said it prefers to remain independent and is resisting the offer.
Loewen filed a lawsuit against Service Corp., alleging its unsolicited bid would substantially reduce competition in the market for funeral services.
The Federal Trade Commission, the Canadian Competition Bureau and officials in several U.S. states have launched investigations into the potential antitrust implications of a deal, Loewen said.

The Texas federal court found Service Corp. filed its lawsuit on the same day its board decided to make a hostile bid for Loewen's stock and before the offer was announced or even made known to Loewen officials, Loewen said.
Service Corp. officials were not immediately available to comment.
